correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the argument on the real rank-exactly-one manifold. The entrywise weights are in [1,kappa] and attain both endpoints, so Eckart–Young plus the nonnegative added weight establishes the unique global minimum at X_a. The X_22 nonzero chart makes the only potentially indefinite quadratic block the pair (X_12,X_21), with Hessian eigenvalues kappa±a/b. At equality setting both to z and X_22=b-kappa z^2/b cancels the quadratic and yields quartic coefficient (1-kappa^2)/(2b^2)<0. In dimension two, det is a regular constraint off the zero matrix. A critical matrix with a nonzero off-diagonal must have multiplier ±kappa. The plus sign gives two negative diagonals and uv=-u^2, contradicting their positive product. The minus sign gives the stated x_*,y_*, with u=v and xy>0 precisely in the asserted strict regime; the restricted Hessian on the positive-diagonal branch has both signs. For the barrier, every continuous path crosses X_11=x_* with 0<x_*<b/kappa<a. There uv=x_*y and weighted AM–GM gives the lower bound at that slice; minimizing over signed y yields y_*=b-kappa x_*>0. The path y=(b-kappa x)_+ with both off-diagonals sqrt(xy) stays nonzero and rank one, and its two quadratic pieces peak globally at x_*. The peak increment over f(X_b) is exactly (kappa b-a)^2/(2(kappa^2-1)). This proof excludes lower-cost bypasses outside the leading block, including nonsymmetric or signed paths.
residual_risks: The critical-point census applies only to N=2. Finite symbolic/rational identities do not prove census exhaustiveness or the path lower bound; those are analytic.

value.rationale: The exact relationship between conditioning and the two leading singular values shows why nearly ideal conditioning alone does not prevent trapping in a rank-underfit SPD matrix equation. The quartic at equality and the exact barrier, provably not lowered by going through extra coordinates, distinguish this from a routine witness of one nonglobal stationary point.
residual_risks: The operator is diagonal in matrix units with two Kronecker-product terms; this does not quantify the landscape of arbitrary SPD operators or predict the convergence of a particular algorithm.
